data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Shimon, meaning 'he who hears.' In Christianity, Saint Simon was a fisherman who became a disciple of Jesus. The name Simonetta carries the meaning “God hears” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Simonetta usually hope their child will grow to embody god hears and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Simonetta total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Simonetta Vespucci, an Italian woman believed to be the model for the Mona Lisa, was born in Florence around 1453. She was a member of the prominent Vespucci family and was known for her great beauty. Her nickname was 'La Belissima' or 'the most beautiful'.

Saint Simonetta of Siena, a laywoman and mystic, lived in the late 14th century in Siena, Italy. She was known for her deep devotion to the Madonna and her ecstatic visions. She was later canonized by the Catholic Church and is now remembered as a saint.

modern_usage.modern_context: Simonetta Vespucci (circa 1453-1476) was an Italian woman of the Renaissance period, famous for her great beauty. Her name is often associated with the ideal of female beauty during this time. In Italian art history, she is considered a muse for various artists, including Sandro Botticelli, who painted her as the Primavera. On Instagram, there are numerous accounts dedicated to her beauty and influence, with users sharing images of her depictions, modern interpretations, and inspirations. On Pinterest, there are boards dedicated to 'Renaissance beauty' and 'Simonetta Vespucci', showcasing various images, quotes, and articles about her. The modern context of Simonetta's name extends beyond art and history to fashion and beauty, where it is used as a trendy name for clothing and cosmetic products.
